content.content:
1	# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline
2	
3	Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
4	cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.
5	
6	## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)
7	
8	- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
9	  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
10	  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
11	- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
12	  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
13	  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
14	  auditing, and mechanical verification.
15	- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
16	  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
17	  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.
18	
19	## Main-session context hygiene
20	
21	- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
22	  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
23	  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
24	  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
25	- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
26	  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
27	  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
28	- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
29	  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
30	  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
31	- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
32	  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
33	  context is already large.
34	
35	## This machine runs concurrent sessions
36	
37	Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
38	one session on 2026-09-04:
39	
40	- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
41	  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
42	  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
43	  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
44	  whose destination only they know.
45	- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
46	  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
47	  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
48	  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
49	  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.
50	
51	`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
52	reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
53	`npx vite preview`.
54	
55	Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:
56	
57	- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
58	  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
59	  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
60	  one shell instead of polling.
61	- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
62	  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
63	  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
64	  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
65	  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
66	  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
67	- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
68	  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
69	  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
70	- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
71	  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
72	  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
73	  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.
74	
75	## Creative triad
76	
77	For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
78	polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
79	Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
80	contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
81	timeline files or approve their own implementation.
82	
83	Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
84	directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
85	checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.
86	
87	Durable contracts live in:
88	
89	- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
90	- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
91	- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
92	  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
93	- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
94	- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`
95	
96	## Story scope
97	
98	Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
99	gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
100	story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the
101	space-station chapter. Do not refuse or defer this work on the basis of an
102	older freeze — earlier revisions of this file carried one, and it expired.
103	
104	What still applies:
105	
106	- **Creative-Triad and registry gates are the remaining barrier** between a new

# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the
space-station chapter. Do not refuse or defer this work on the basis of an
older freeze — earlier revisions of this file carried one, and it expired.

What still applies:

- **Creative-Triad and registry gates are the remaining barrier** between a new
  chapter and the runtime. Route the work through them; do not route around.
- **Sequencing is owner-directed: do not rush to the station.** Making the
  existing story enjoyable comes first, and the need to leave must emerge from
  play rather than from a new content hook.
- **The demo's release surface is unchanged** — it still stops at
  `ch4-arrival`, and publishing remains a separate decision. Building past it
  is allowed; shipping it in the demo is not implied.
- **Shipped copy and audio remain protected baselines.** Changing a protected
  audio/runtime path is still a contracted change, not an incidental one.
- **"Anchorage" is retired as a name.** The location is the **space station**.

2

5	Contract target: Common Ground, run `2026-09-05-after-the-hearth`. This is a derived intent, not a scene signature or production-readiness claim.
6	
7	## Grounding
8	
9	This translates the signed council direction into production requirements. It is not another treatment, canon decision, dispatch or signature. Governing council directory: `../../story-runs/2026-09-06-common-ground/`.

13	- Exact three-director signatures, `owner-story-decision.json`, `director-notes.json`, and accepted `chapter-reconciliation.json` supply the reconciled authority. The producer exercised standing user delegation, not personal owner review of future hashes/media.

These converge on the backed instrument, necessary reciprocal comparison and explicit final occupied reference. They are proposed council-v2 content, not already signed amendments to the hashes above.
17	
18	**Current measured world, accurately limited.** `geometry-pass2.md/json` correct pass 1's rays through unrendered voxels. The original flat corridor's 68/64-unit routes, two primary trunk-hidden samples and start-position witness were dramatically insufficient. The final `geometry-arena.md/json` supersedes intermediate water-search reports: two real dry banks and a +16-unit / 1.44-times detour exist. Topology did not cause that proposal's failure. Across 20,000 evaluated combinations, at range 12 the fully covered longer route coexisted with at most two unsupported short-route units; a short gap of at least six left the longer route at best 94.03% covered. At range 24, a fully covered longer route left no unsupported short gap. No witness/common stage was reached. The new opaque backing supplies an explicit physical reference blind side; no water, terrain-relief or optional-foliage claim supplies it.
19	
20	The shared voxel planner omits the real trunk collider. `commonGroundRoute.ts` must layer injected actual-solid guards over the unchanged planner; the instrument's rendered backing, walking collision and reference-ray solid must agree. Never exempt the whole housing from a reference ray or inflate its collider into a hidden wall.
21	
22	Cinema's `cinema-targeted-baseline.md` and the independent `targeted-baseline-report.md/json` report 11 current frames: seven Origin rehearsals with W-7744 absent, and four Tidegarden rehearsals with no built core mesh despite the seeded marker/receipts. They establish current world context and expose fixture limits. They do not show ch13 actor/core/apparatus blocking. Their software-rendered, requested-low-tier frames do not establish hardware, motion, audio or actual quality-tier acceptance. Chapter has read those reports, not personally viewed or accepted the frames.
23	
24	Seen world context plus source geometry grounds this direction. New body, restored-core, trace and apparatus blocking, live-edited terrain, day/night and tier interaction proof belong **after signed implementation**. Do not demand a precontract render of a state that does not exist. Only three measured bindings remain open in this draft: **selected nominated range, the complete rigid world placement, and its evidence hash**. Council-v2 judgment/adoption and the separately signed scene contract remain workflow gates before the planning-only lock can open; these are not routine owner-permission questions.
25	
26	## Bounded apparatus and measured bindings
27	
28	One fixed passive, nonluminous field reference has a visible finite scale and opaque rear housing. This finite useful range is a **new instrument design**, not existing physics or a perceptual awakening. The reference socket projects ahead of the backing; real solid geometry creates the blind side. Held references visibly lack that backing but obey the same socket-to-socket range and solid-sightline rule. No invisible cone, placed-stake quota, new facility or worldgen change.
29	
30	The one CPU comparison evaluates these two already nominated local layouts, rigidly translated and quarter-turned as a whole onto actual dry Origin support. Local Y=0 denotes grounded pose, not a world elevation. No independent coordinate tuning is implied.
31	
32	| Nomination | Start S | Survey end E | Intermediate witness W | Worker final arrival C | Common E→C length |
33	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
34	| Range 24 | (-16,0,-16) | (-16,0,16) | (-18,0,0) | (-16,0,28) | 12 units |
35	| Range 12 | (-8,0,-8) | (-8,0,8) | (-9,0,0) | (-8,0,14) | 6 units |
36	
37	Both use fixed socket R=(0,1.30,0); backing center=(-0.90,1.30,0), thickness X=0.12, height Y=2.00, width Z=1.60, with visible bracket and supported stand. Worker socket is 1.85 and player socket 1.35 above their grounded poses. Only planar S/E/W/C offsets are halved; body sizes, housing, heights and occupancy tolerances are unchanged. C is **his** arrival point. Terra's final occupied reference is a separate reachable dry position beside C, nominated lateral offset at least two units, unscaled; actual body and route clearance remains the predicate, not a two-unit exemption. Her permitted movement can safely hold him if it blocks his path.
38	
39	The proof must retain both caps and show: independently covered longer route at least 12 units **and** 25% longer; at least six contiguous unsupported walking units on the shorter survey route; inadequate start/end witnesses under the same honest rule; useful intermediate witness; and the full reciprocal exchange. E→C needs a **nonzero** portion outside the original fixed reference's useful coverage while entirely supported by W-7744 at E. The six-unit unsupported threshold applies only to the shorter survey route, not to the common span's portion outside fixed range. The coordinates 14/28 name C's local Z, not an extra out-of-range-distance requirement. Select only a measured valid nomination; a failure cannot be hidden by relaxing these terms.
40	
41	## Dramatic contract
42	
43	- **Player action:** choose Origin from a working home; walk and offer a trace; inspect a specific hold; revise the untested tail or hold an intermediate reference; use W-7744's reference for her own comparison; explicitly offer and occupy the far reference for his independent test.
44	- **Before → after:** Terra treats having crossed as having finished the proof → she accepts another body's necessary contribution to a result she wants, while their accounts remain different.
45	- **Information:** W-7744 repeats his unresolved local measurement and retains `LOCAL RECORD: PASSAGE OBSERVED. MODEL INCOMPLETE.`
46	- **Ambiguity:** his interiority, larger allegiance and later awakening remain unknown. Local usefulness is not friendship.
47	- **Both readings:** a worker and an embodied route intelligence learn from another body's evidence without cosmology disclosure or erasing Worker 9.
48	- **Tutorial:** distinguish traversability from demonstrability; learn reversible trace revision and reference occupancy maintained by either body.
49	- **Ceiling:** `alive` on all four beats, resume, diagnostic entry and completed visits. Gain a practical reading of relationships, not greater world fidelity.
50	
51	## Character and causal spine
52	
53	| Presence | Desire / opposition | Tactic | Belief before → after | Visible evidence |
54	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
55	| Terra | Obtain a route whose limits she can rely on; she cannot walk and hold its reference simultaneously | Demonstrate, revise or hold, then depend on his maintained measurement | My crossing finished the proof → I needed the end he held | Her otherwise incomplete comparison becomes possible through his actual reference, then hers supports his test |
56	| W-7744 | Repeat his failed measurement; living terrain exceeds the record | Test, hold for a literal reason, hold the other end, make his final test | Record limits action → local record can admit incompleteness | Grounded movement and kept annotation; no interior monologue |
57	| Worker 9 / third consciousness | Existing long arc and protected evidence grammar | No new attributed voice, act or motif | No new player-facing claim | Deliberate absence of identity evidence |
58	
59	## Reveal and payoff ledger
60	
61	| Decision | Before → after | Setup / payoff | Preserve |
62	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
63	| CG-D01/02 | Mechanical repair → acknowledged home and explicit return choice | Existing cell install → stored-fault review | No new fault, summons, extra cell or knowledge of his location |
64	| CG-D03 | A4 retreat/fault → visible local reinspection | Existing fault → repeated measure | Protected later offworld/A5 return question; no rejected report, dispatch or tracking |
65	| CG-D04/05 | No shared route → real comparison and incomplete local record | Chosen trace → his independent arrival | No alliance, network clearance or conversion |
66	| CG-D06/07 | Personal route → two complete retained route classes | Reference tests → optional Origin repeat | No gaze gate, moral ranking or disappearing tester |
67	| CG-D08/09/10 | Existing alive voices/world/score → relational reading | Sensory parentheses, bare owned intent, procedural worker | Zero new hidden-pillar nudge; preserve A5 Light and all later reveals |
68	
69	The candidate's eight approved lines remain the original copy source. The bounded amendments add `i walked it. i thought that finished the proof.` before Terra's comparison and `i needed the end he held.` after its actual completion. No forced failed crossing is needed. This cost is relinquishing unilateral completion, with no new threat or confession. New sensory/involuntary thought is lowercase parenthetical; deliberate intent is bare lowercase; W-7744 stays procedural caps. The old fault remains visibly archived, without a transmission cue. Existing chapter copy is unchanged. “Survey end” replaces the proposed “far shore” only in new-chapter guidance because the backed apparatus does not depend on a shore destination.
70	
71	## Beat and agency ledger
72	
73	| Beat / boundary | Shared anchors | Cause and playable event | Agency / hold / retry | Handback and acceptance |
74	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
75	| External ch11/ch12 | CG-B0 live install; restored-entry steady state | Real station departure, flight, landing, one-cell installation | Shipped actions; pending saves preserve progress; restored saves skip transaction/transient | Return objective/acknowledgement retires; home keeps working |
76	| `ch13-home` | CG-01 return chosen | At the real restored Tidegarden core, review the stored fault, then choose to revisit Origin | Invitation can remain pending; explicit F accepts; no night wait, autoaccept or teleport | Hatch/course guidance only after choice; build mode keeps F |
77	| `ch13-return` | Origin returned; CG-02 repeated measure | Actual board/lift/cross/land/disembark and approach | Existing vehicle/player controls; no repeated dock or reseed | Actor offer at actual physical reach |
78	| `ch13-survey` | CG-03 offer; contingent CG-04 hold; revision/witness resume | Walked trace becomes a physical proposal | Both routes complete; first-try success legal; specific reference/footing failure; tested prefix survives | Earned facts lead to reciprocal phase |
79	| `ch13-common` | CG-05 other end; CG-06 his test; CG-07 completion; CG-08 open ground | W-7744 holds E while Terra checks E→C; Terra explicitly offers a separate far reference; he independently tests E→C | Each body supplies a currently necessary reference. Missing occupancy/range/sight/clearance safely holds; looking away is free | Actual arrival plus reciprocal proof commits once; mandatory guidance retires and full controls/progression immediately free |
80	
81	Preserve all four formal beats. Use the explicitly typed external station/return transition, existing ch11/ch12 receipts and strict direct registry adjacency. Ch10 cannot acquire a false restored-home guarantee. The movie must depart through the actual station UI/action, retain screening intent without `story=` reseeding, physically return/install and accept the invitation. Rails use the same walking, F, reference and actor predicates. Timeout means stuck, never completion. Direct-entry diagnostics seed physical prerequisites explicitly and do not prove the continuous bridge.

This corrects the interface plan's stray “on-foot Origin” entry wording. A dormant completed save must reach the invitation reliably without replaying a cell transaction. Receipt-only debug seeding cannot claim a built core. All resume clauses precede ch10's done fallback and return `alive` explicitly.
84	
85	## Executable objective lifecycle
86	
87	One objective and exact matching active marker own each required verb/target. Use existing F rising-edge arbitration and touch glyph substitution. Fine flight substeps keep current controls and split guidance when the actual action changes.
88	
89	| Objective ID | Exact marker label | Standing work order | Real transition |
90	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
91	| `station:return:tidegarden` | TIDEGARDEN · SECOND HEARTH | RETURN TO TIDEGARDEN. DELIVER THE BONDED CELL TO THE SECOND HEARTH. | Existing world/flight predicate selects install |
92	| `hearth:return:install-cell` | SECOND HEARTH · INSTALL BONDED CELL | DELIVER THE BONDED CELL TO THE SECOND HEARTH. [F] INSTALL THE SEALED CELL. | Consume one; existing ch12 receipts; one live acknowledgement |
93	| `ch13:home:review` | Second hearth · unfinished audit | Return to the working hearth. [F] Review the stored audit fault. | Actual core review → choose-return |
94	| `ch13:home:choose-return` | Second hearth · choose the return | [F] Choose to revisit the Origin audit site. You can leave this open. | Intent commit → actual hatch/course substep |
95	| `ch13:return:board` | Kestrel hatch · board | Follow the hatch marker. [F] Board the Kestrel. | Actual boarded state → launch/current flight substep |
96	| `ch13:return:launch` | Kestrel controls · lift | Hold [Space] to ignite and lift. | Actual flight → Origin course |
97	| `ch13:return:origin` | Origin · audit site | Fly to Origin. Follow the audit-site approach and land. | Actual world/grounded flight facts → disembark/approach |
98	| `ch13:survey:offer` | W-7744 · offer a route | Approach W-7744. [F] Offer to demonstrate a route. | Open actor/world-scoped survey → draw |
99	| `ch13:survey:draw` | Survey end · demonstrate a route | Walk your route to the survey end. [F] Offer the recorded span. | Grounded samples form proposal, not accepted proof |
100	| `ch13:survey:offer-span` | Trace end · offer this span | [F] Offer the walked span for W-7744 to test. | Explicit offer plus valid finite trace → test |
101	| `ch13:survey:test` | W-7744 · test in progress | W-7744 is testing the offered route. Follow his progress, or return to the last tested point to revise. | Actual worker samples → hold/next span/reciprocal |
102	| `ch13:survey:revise` | Last tested point · revise route | Return to the last tested point. [F] Reopen the untested span and walk a new route. | Reopen unverified tail → draw; include actual refusal reason |
103	| `ch13:survey:witness` | Witness point · hold this end | Stand at the marked reference. [F] Offer this end, then remain here while W-7744 tests the span. Looking around is free. | Offer + occupancy + valid geometry maintains test |
104	| `ch13:survey:witness-return` | Witness point · resume the test | Return to the marked reference to resume the test. To change the route, return to the last tested point. | Reenter inner cylinder and revalidate; no second F |

106	| `ch13:common:offer-final-reference` | Far reference · offer this end | Stand at the far reference, clear of the tested span. [F] Offer this end. | Explicit valid offer replaces guidance; does not commit his test |
107	| `ch13:common:release` | Far reference · keep this end | Remain at the far reference while W-7744 tests the span. Looking around is free. | Current reference/range/visibility and body clearance permit independent movement; actual arrival plus comparison commits once |
108	| `ch13:common:reference-return` | Far reference · resume the test | Return to the far reference, clear of the tested span, to resume the test. Looking around is free. | Reentry and actual revalidation resume without another F; retained proof alone cannot move him |

110	Draw targets the survey destination; offer-span replaces it with the actual trace end when that is the actionable target. Never change a marker behind an unchanged objective. Continuous walking retains one quiet work order: no sample/turn prompt, chime or congratulatory microstep. Alternative nearby actions use the same resolver without competing required markers.

112	Each entry has one semantic acknowledgement, actual trace growth shows progress without per-sample chimes, invalid input has a literal reason, and commits clear/replace old guidance within the existing UX frame contract. Exact frame bands remain scene-contract evidence work. Restore is silent. Missing/unmounted targets expose preparation or world-return state rather than a zero-coordinate marker. Live installation retires its objective and acknowledgement before publishing the invitation; this is a presentation boundary, never an audio/listening prerequisite. Restored saves get steady state only. No required action depends solely on a transient caption.

114	## World-reference, persistence and reset constraints

116	The longer survey route uses the fixed reference throughout; the shorter needs one occupied intermediate reference through the actual housing shadow. Both are complete equal outcomes, with no moral or musical ranking and no forced failed first attempt. Test actual grounded samples in the offered corridor under current worker dry/top-face/slope/clearance rules. Replanning cannot cut across the demonstrated argument. Save the chosen survey class separately from the common reciprocal comparison.

60:  'scene-contract.json',
78:const JOURNEY_CONTRACT_REPO_REF = 'main/chapter-journey-contract.json'
79:const JOURNEY_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_REPO_REF = 'docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/schemas/paravoxia-chapter-journey-contract.schema.json'
149:  const contractPath = path.join(runPath, 'scene-contract.json')
374:  const anchorOrders = new Map((contract.syncAnchors || []).map((anchor) => [anchorId(anchor), anchor?.order]))
375:  const contractResetTriggers = new Set(contract.reset?.triggers || [])
400:  collector.assert(contract.schema === 'paravoxia.sceneContract.v1', 'contract.schema', 'Scene contract schema must be paravoxia.sceneContract.v1')
401:  collector.assert(nonEmptyString(contract.sceneId), 'contract.scene-id', 'Scene contract must declare a stable sceneId')
402:  collector.assert(nonEmptyString(contract.contractVersion), 'contract.version', 'Scene contract must declare contractVersion')
403:  collector.assert(contract.status === 'frozen', 'contract.status', 'A gateable scene contract must be frozen')
404:  collector.assert(isObject(contract.production), 'contract.production', 'Scene contract must include production authority')
405:  collector.assert(Array.isArray(contract.production?.authorityRefs) && contract.production.authorityRefs.length > 0, 'contract.authority', 'Production authorityRefs are required')
406:  collector.assert(nonEmptyString(contract.production?.productionLockRef), 'contract.production-lock', 'Production lock reference is required')
407:  collector.assert(['delta', 'scene', 'chapter', 'flagship'].includes(contract.production?.mode), 'contract.mode', 'Production mode must be delta, scene, chapter, or flagship')
408:  collector.assert(['planning-only', 'bounded-runtime', 'full-scene-runtime'].includes(contract.production?.mutationBoundary), 'contract.mutation-boundary', 'Mutation boundary must be explicit')
409:  collector.assert(Array.isArray(contract.production?.allowedPaths), 'contract.allowed-paths', 'Allowed paths must be explicit')
410:  collector.assert(Array.isArray(contract.production?.protectedPaths), 'contract.protected-paths', 'Protected paths must be explicit')
411:  collector.assert(Array.isArray(contract.scope?.beats) && contract.scope.beats.length > 0, 'contract.beats', 'At least one affected beat is required')
412:  collector.assert(Array.isArray(contract.scope?.shippedReferenceRefs) && contract.scope.shippedReferenceRefs.length > 0, 'contract.references', 'At least one shipped reference is required')
413:  collector.assert(Array.isArray(contract.story?.events) && contract.story.events.length > 0, 'contract.story-events', 'Story events are required')
414:  collector.assert(Array.isArray(contract.story?.agencyWindows) && contract.story.agencyWindows.length > 0, 'contract.agency', 'Player agency windows are required')

# Scene-contract assembly notes

Producer mechanical preparation, 2026-09-06. `scene-contract.assembly.json` is a
DRAFT (`status: draft`, `contractVersion: scene-v1`) awaiting lane review. It
claims no approval, no runtime authority, no signature and no measured result.
The active `scene-contract.json`, the lock, signatures, source, schema,
validator and director-owned treatments were not modified.

## Validation performed

Ajv is not installed in this repo, so the file was checked with a local
draft-subset validator against the checked-in scene-contract schema, plus a
mirror of the gate's structural reference, guidance-lifecycle, placeholder and
band-prose checks. Result: 0 schema errors; 1 mirrored gate failure (below).
Every `evidenceRefs`, authority, palette, cut and probe path resolves today.

## Open, unbound and conflicting fields

1. `ux.contract-work-order` fails for `station:return:tidegarden`: its exact
   shipped last line, "DELIVER THE BONDED CELL TO THE SECOND HEARTH.", contains
   no verb in the gate's `travel` lexicon. Copy was preserved rather than
